full_judgment:
Fazle Munim J. — This Rule was directed against an order dated 12. 3. 73 passed by the government by which the lands in question; were withdrawn from acquisition under section 8B of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948. The petitioner who is the owner and proprietor of Stall No. 185 of the Chittagong Development Authority, New Market Hawker's Market, Jubilee Road, Chittagong, took lease of Commercial plots No.1 and 2 from the Chittagong Development Authority (which I will call 'the authority') for the purpose of constructing a stall thereon. Like the petitioner 2 other Hawkers were also allotted plots on the lands in question and they have been carrying on their business after constructing shops and stalls in their respective plots. As nearly as 22. 6. 66 an area of land measuring 68 acre bearing plot Nos. 1197, 1200, 1205, 1206, 1207 and 1208 of mouza Batali within the police station kotwali, Chittagong was requisitioned by the government under section of the East Bengal (Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (which I will call 'the Act)' for construction of Chittagong new market for development of Commercial Area in and around Jubilee Road, Chittagong. The scheme No. 5 which was prepared by the authority for the construction of the market was duly approved by the government. After requisitioning, the aforesaid lands were handed over to the authority in December, 1967. The lands were subsequently acquired by the government on 30.6.70 under sub-section 7 of Section 5 of the said Act and finally on 21. 10. 70 for the aforesaid scheme of the authority. After developing the land in question the Chittagong development authority earmarked the same plots for setting up a Hawker's Market in order to rehabilitate the displaced persons who were evicted from the road side. The petitioner who was a Hawker was allotted his present plot. After the allotment of the plot of land measuring 55.90 sq. fit. The petitioner constructed his shop on the said plot. The authority also executed a deed of lease with the petitioner on 16.9.71 which was registered on 28. 9. 71. The authority also executed similar deeds of lease with other allottees. After the acquisition of the land in question in 1970 as mentioned above final payment of compensation money has been made to almost all the awardees. Out of total compensation money of Tk. 1, 72,552.31 paisa an amount of Taka 1, 12,573.60 paisa has already been paid. On 20. 4. 74 a copy of the letter addressed by the then Chairman of the authority to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong was sent to the Secretary, New Hawker's Market Dokandar Samity from which the petitioner learnt about the decision to withdraw the land in question from acquisition. The letter as contained in Annexure 'B' to the petition is as follows :- 

 Sub: - Withdrawal from Acquisition of land belonging to K. B. Abdul Aziz Waqf Estate. 

 His attention is invited to the Ministry of Works Memo No. (CS-XV)3P-3/73/420E dt. 4th April, 1974 copy endorsed to him. In accepting the undertaking, given by Mr. Mahmud Nurul Huda, Mutawalli, K. B. A. Aziz Waqf Estate it is requested that necessary action may kindly be taken to withdraw from acquisition vide L. A. Case No. 21/55-66, the following quantities of land scheduled below as per plan enclosed. 

 On further enquiry the petitioner came to learned that the government had already passed an order of the withdrawal of the land from acquisition under section 8B of the Act. This letter which is addressed, to the Deputy Commissioner Chittagong on 12. 3. 73 is as follows: 

 In forwarding herewith a copy of this Ministry's Memo No. Ch.-85/70/84-Regn, dated 19. 2. 73 addressed to Mr. Mahmud Nurul Huda, Mutwalli of K. B. Abdul Aziz Waqf Estate, Chittagong. On the subject mentioned above, the under signed is directed to say that government have been pleased to agree to withdraw from acquisition u/s. 8B of the East Bengal (Emergency Regn. of Property Act, 1948, the land measuring above 3343 of an acre out of 68 of an acre of land acquired under Notification No..Ch-85/70/ 737-Regn. dated 30. 6. 70 and as amended under Corrigendum No. Ch-85/70/1176- Regn. dated 21. 10. 70 on the terms and conditions as laid down in the memo mentioned above. 

 The Mutwalli of the Waqf Estate has already accepted the terms and conditions and furnished an undertaking accordingly as desired by government. A copy of the said undertaking is enclosed herewith. 

 2. Mr. M. H. Khandker, the learned Advocate for the petitioner referred to the provision of section 8B of the Act. His objections to the order of withdrawal are several. First, the government had no authority to withdraw any property from acquisition after the payment of compensation money. Secondly, there has been no gazette notification of the order withdrawing the land in question from acquisition. Thirdly, the lands in question did not vest in respondent No. 6 because in passing an order for withdrawal of the lands in question from the acquisition the government imposed certain conditions which will be presently seen. Fourthly, since the petitioner's right to property was affected the Government was under the legal duty to serve a show cause notice upon him which has not been done in the present case. Fifthly, no reasons appears from the impugned order of withdrawal why the lands in question are being withdrawn from acquisition, particularly when no objection was made against the order of requisition or no appeal was preferred against the acquisition. - For, he mentioned that the lands in question were requisitioned nearly 8 years ago and acquired nearly 4 years ago before the impugned order was made. 

 3. Mr. B. B. Roy Choudhury, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1, and 3, submitted that the government had authority to withdraw the lands in question from acquisition and the decision to withdraw being administrative in nature its propriety cannot be questioned. Secondly, the impugned order allows that the petitioners' rights, whatever they are, have been protected by the Government and as such he cannot have any cause for grievance against the impugned order. In the beginning, however, he had submitted that the petitioners' rights were not affected by the impugned order. 

 4. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 6 in whose favor the impugned order stands submitted that as early as February, 1969 the lands in question were derequisitioned by the Govt. At that time the authority raised objections against derequisition but the Govt. did not maintain the order of derequisition. In his opinion, therefore, the subsequent acquisition by the Govt. has been illegal. 

 5. As regards the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner it appears that the power to withdraw any property from acquisition is subject to certain limitations imposed by section 8B of the Act. The chief limitation is intended to be the fact whether compensation has been paid or not. If compensation has not been paid the order of withdrawal may be made but since finality must attach to the proceeding for requisition and acquisition, no such withdrawal can be ordered after compensation has been made. The words limiting the power of the government to withdraw any property from acquisition are contained in the words "at any time before the payment of compensation". If the Govt. had the power to withdraw any property from acquisition after compensation has been made there would be no finality to the acquisition proceedings nor any sanctity would attach to the government order acquiring any property. Any person who might have acquired any right to any property after the acquisition of such property by the government and after compensation has been paid for such acquisition can be deprived of it as there would be no sanctity attached to such right. We think that for these reasons the Govt's choice to withdraw any property from acquisition as conferred by section 8B of the Act must be exercised before the payment of compensation and not after it. The Second limitation is that such order of withdrawal must be done by a Notification published in the official gazette. This requirement as laid down, by section 8B has not been fulfilled in the present case. Though the aforesaid section has provided that after the order of withdrawal the property shall vest back in the owner in the rights which he had before such property were acquired, it appears from the following letter dt. 19. 2. 73 that the property did not so vest. The letter which is contained in Annexure "B" to the affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the respondent No. 6 is as follows :- 

 Mr. Muhammad Nurul Huda, Mutwalli of K. B. Abdul Azif Waqf Estate. 

 With reference to his representation dated 19.7.72 addressed to the Ministry in-charge, of Land Administration and Land Reforms, Govt. of Bangladesh, praying for release and restoration of properties of the Waqf Estate from Acquisition the undersigned is directed to inform him that after due consideration of his objection against acquisition of the land said to be belonging to the Waqf Estate, the Govt. in the interest of the Waqf Estate has been considering to withdraw from acquisition u/s. 8B of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, the land measuring about 3343 of an acre out of 68 of an acre of land acquired u/s. 5(7) of the Act, under Notification No.737-Reqn., dated 30. 6. 70 provided the Waqf Estate is agreed to accept the following terms and conditions:- 

 (1) That the Waqf Estate shall not claim restoration and physical possession of the land after withdrawal. 

 (2) That the waqf Estate shall have to accept the existing hawkers as its tenants on the same terms and conditions already imposed on them by the CDA and shall not disturb them in their possession and present avocations. 

 (3) That the Waqf Estate shall pay the cost of development and other charges already incurred by the CDA and shall agree to pay, betterment fees, if any, charged by the CDA. 

 (4) That the Waqf Estate shall refund the Cost of acquisition, if any, received by them from the Deputy Commissioner under L.A. Case No. 21/65/-66. 

 If the above terms and conditions are accepted by the Waqf Estate, he is requested to furnish an undertaking accordingly on a Non-judicial Stamp paper of Taka 1/50 (Taka one and fifty paisa) at an early date. 

 Of the four terms and conditions laid down in this letter the first two show that the property could not vest in respondent No. 6, in the rights which he had in such property before it was acquired. First, he cannot claim restoration and physical possession of the land. Secondly, he had to accept the existing hawkers as its tenants on the same terms and condition as imposed upon them by the authority. These two conditions show that the government was not in a position to give the property back in the condition in which it was before the acquisition nor could it give the respondent No. 6 all the rights which he had in it before the acquisition. Apart from this aspect, it is clear from the provisions of section 8B that the government had no power to impose such terms and conditions on the owner at the time it ordered the withdrawal of the property from acquisition. Section 8B rather positively indicates that the owner should get back the property with all the rights he had before the property was acquired by the government. Since the petitioner is an allottee of a portion of the lands in question which were handed over to the Authority he was entitled to receive a show cause notice before the order of withdrawal was made. 

 7. Before we part with the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner it remains to be stated that the impugned order does not indicate any reason why the lands in question were being withdrawn from acquisition after the entire proceedings of acquisition were completed as early as 21.10.70 as mentioned above. If neither the requisition nor the acquisition of the lands in question were challenged by the respondent No. 6 nor any appeal was preferred against the order of acquisition why all on a sudden nearly three years after: the acquisition the order of withdrawal was made has remained unexplained. When such extraordinary order was being made after such a lapse of time and after handing over the land in question to the authority which in its turn allotted them to as nearly as 212 allottees, some extraordinary reasons should have existed before making such an order. No such reasons are forthcoming. Moreover, it appears from the letter dated 4. 6. 66 written by the respondents No. 6 to the Chairman of the Authority that he had no objection to such acquisition but would be glad if a portion of the land was allotted to him subject to paying premium and other things so far as it relates to the allotment of such lands. Also from the letter dated 8. 1. 68 written by the Chairman of the Authority to the government it appears that the authority was unwilling to release the land as it would upset the entire scheme prepared by the Authority and would lead to serious complications in the matter of implementation of the scheme. He also mentioned in his letter that concession was shown to the Waqf Estate by allotting two plots to it. 

 8. Referring to the terms and conditions which were imposed on the respondent No. 6 while withdrawal of the lands in question from acquisition was made; Mr. B. B. Roy Chowdhury the learned Assistant Attorney-General, submitted that the first two terms and conditions as contained in the Govt. letter dated 19.2.73, which has been quoted above, showed that the Govt. was not unmindful of the petitioner's right. It, therefore, amply protected his right by imposing those conditions on the respondent No. 6. In addition to what has already been said above it may be mentioned that such terms and conditions are in the eye of law ineffective because the Govt. had no authority under the provisions' of section 8B to impose such terms and conditions on the owner of the property to when it was being returned. Moreover, there is no indication as to how long these terms and conditions would be affective Further, why should be petitioner agree to accept such terms and conditions or be willing to become a tenant under the respondent No. 6. There can be no analogy between the ordinary transfers of property with tenants thereon and the order of withdrawal passed by the govt. under section 8Bof the Act. The reasons for the reluctance of the petitioner to accept the position as disclosed in the letter dated 19. 2. 73 can more easily be perceived than, expressed. 

 9. So far as the submission made by Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.6, it suffices to say that we are not hearing any objection regarding the validity of the acquisition of the property concerned. If the respondent No. 6 had any grievances against the authority regarding the acquisition of the land in question be should have proceeded differently. We are unable to entertain any objection regarding the validity of the acquisition proceedings.
